entries.symbol: Startup move of action items and decisions to flat ids
entries.behavior: Once startup content settles, moves every stored action item and decision whose id has a colon ("board:<id>", "inbox:<source>:<entity>", "<conversation>:<type>:<n>:<hash>"), which directory sync stores as nested folders, to its flat id, keeping content, visibility and timestamps. A hand-added card is named after its title. A move that stopped after writing the flat id is finished on the next start.
entries.currentConsumers: Action items and decisions stored in deployed brains and their synced content repos before flat ids.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored action items or decisions with a colon in their id across supported upgrade sources.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before flat ids derives colon ids again, so it can take an Inbox item onto the board twice or re-add a conversation card the board already owns.

entries.behavior: Reads action items stored before the frontmatter trim: takes capturedAt from timeRange.end, flattens nested-identity people to { name, id, aliases }, and ignores spaceId, sourceSummaryId, sourceMessageCount and projectionVersion. The next write stores the trimmed shape.
entries.currentConsumers: Action items stored in deployed brains before the trim.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored action items carrying a retired field or a nested person across supported upgrade sources, or rewrite them in place.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before the trim reads only the old shape; items rewritten in the trimmed shape need the forward release.

entries.behavior: Preserves timestamp-only capture claims without automatically replaying them; new captures use atomic entity mutation receipts.
entries.currentConsumers: Persisted faq.captured-replies entries that cannot distinguish completed captures from interrupted attempts.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Explicitly reconcile all existing claims into verified durable dispositions or retire them with owner approval, and stop all old claim writers. Age alone cannot prove completion.
entries.rollbackDependency: Retain existing claims to avoid counting historical completed captures twice. New receipts are not understood by older runtimes; rolling back capture code requires disabling capture or a separately verified downgrade plan.

entries.behavior: Reads old topic fields and strips the retired Sources body section.
entries.currentConsumers: Topic markdown created before the canonical topic schema.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Rewrite supported topic stores to the canonical schema and observe zero old fields or Sources sections.
entries.rollbackDependency: Prior topic entities remain readable until the rewrite has passed its rollback window.

entries.behavior: Rejects removed token configuration with an actionable error.

entries.removalPrerequisite: The minimum supported upgrade source no longer documents or accepts either removed field.
entries.rollbackDependency: None; the fields are already rejected.

entries.behavior: Read-only checks recognize the current Changesets 2 prerelease state; a reviewed version operation exclusively moves consumed Markdown into the Changesets 3 archive and commits the new state last, rolling back ordinary failures.
entries.currentConsumers: The canonical repository's pre-transition pre.json and the parent Git revision used by release-mode classification during the first transition cycle.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Verify the first canonical Changesets 3 version transition and a subsequent release-mode cycle using only the new state shape; then remove the retired state fields and decoder branch.
entries.rollbackDependency: Failure rollback preserves the old state and source bytes. After a successful transition, a tooling downgrade requires a separately reviewed restoration of the old state and archived Markdown; the old CLI cannot consume the new metadata directly.
entries.targetRelease: post-Changesets-3-transition, after one verified release-mode cycle

entries.behavior: Converts retired model and preset configuration into explicit canonical bundles without booting a brain.

entries.removalPrerequisite: Stable 0.2.0 is published and the declared public migration-support window closes.
entries.rollbackDependency: No runtime rollback dependency; retained only for offline upgrades.

entries.behavior: Replaces a previously managed www CNAME when claiming the canonical alias.

entries.removalPrerequisite: Audit supported domains and confirm no managed www CNAME requires in-place replacement.
entries.rollbackDependency: The DNS record remains recoverable from provider history and prior deploy configuration.

entries.behavior: Moves a pilot repo from the single AI_API_KEY to OPENAI_API_KEY: renames aiApiKey selectors and overrides in desired state, the .env.schema variable, the deploy secret list, and the field in overriding users' encrypted secrets.

entries.rollbackDependency: Active desired-state loading never imports it; the pre-migration files stay in the pilot repo's git history.

entries.behavior: Stages retired model/preset or unversioned four-bundle pilot desired state as an isolated capability-bundle review copy, requiring reviewed source-to-target selections and explicit hosted package pins.

entries.removalPrerequisite: Phase 11 reaches zero-drift second reconcile and hosted canaries plus yeehaa.io soak one week on the unified alpha.
entries.rollbackDependency: Retained through the defined crossover rollback horizon; active ops loading never imports it.

The entry also re-exports, unchanged, the shapes a converted service registers and reads with: the Studio workspace and overview contracts and schemas and the admin check a workspace makes for itself, the dashboard widget contracts and operator-view types, the analytics report definition, the Inbox actor and item-list schemas, the channel delivery provider and message response, the app info, health and initial-sync answers, the job request, status and batch-operation types, the API route definition, and the tool helpers (createTool, toolSuccess, toolError and their types). It also re-exports the in-process utilities converted services run on (SerialQueue, SerializedStatusStore, createAdminListTool, and ConfirmationArgsStore, which holds a tool's pending confirmation arguments between its two calls), the config validation error a package throws on a config its schema refuses, and `hasPermission`, the permission rule as a function rather than the PermissionService class. It also makes the entity service's conditional and once-only writes as a class made them through `context.entityService` (`entityMutations`: the write snapshot, a mutation receipt, a mutation applied once under its receipt, a fold, a retired projection rule's ownership released, which topics' one-shot migration runs, and a retired type's records purged with their files, which agent discovery runs for network-piece on every registration, each handed on as written with no check beyond the store's), its distance search (`entityReads.searchWithDistances`) and the records nearest a record by stored embeddings (`entityReads.nearestToEntity`, which topic extraction measures sources with), the brain's semantic space projected around an origin as a class read it through `context.semantic.project` (`entityReads.projectSemanticSpace`, which agent discovery's network_ask and proximity map read), which FAQ capture, merges and folds run on. It also generates through a template named in full as a class generated through `context.ai.generate` (`ai.generate`: the config as written, the result parsed by the call's schema), which topic extraction, votes, descriptions and merges run on. It also reads the brain's conversations as a class read them through `context.conversations` (`conversations`: a conversation's messages in a range, and how many it has, which FAQ capture reads a reply's turns with; one conversation, and the conversations a listing names, which conversation memory's channel pickup, notices and retrieval read; nothing that searches or writes). It also reads the brain's shared conversation spaces as a class read `context.spaces` (`spaces`: the selectors the brain is configured with, frozen), which conversation memory's channel pickup wakes and catches up by. It also serves an entity data source built with defineDataSource over one of the package's own types under the service's id (`serviceRuntime(context).dataSource`), with the runtime's own list, filter, sort, limit, lookup and navigation at the build's scope, as an entity plugin class served it (`agent-discovery:entities`), and refuses one over any other type. It also runs one of the package's own types' projection rules as production runs it, select and derive with no wave, memo or write (`runProjectionRule`), refusing a rule none of its types declares, which skill derivation's and assessment's evals measure the production rule with instead of an eval-only deriver. It also re-exports, for agent discovery, the verified agent-card fetch and its endpoint-refusal check and default timeout, the agent body's format and parse, the anchor profile kind schema and type, the parsed agent card type and the semantic space's point and neighbor types. It also re-exports, for assessment, the agent body type and the skill record's data schema and type its capability profiles read an agent's skills and a derived skill with. It also re-exports, for conversation memory, the conversation and message-actor types and the stored message metadata schema its channel pickup reads a message's speaker and space with, the space selector match its trigger wakes by, the job progress channel and event a finished pickup is heard on, and the permission-to-scope rule its agent context reads memory at. It also re-exports, for topic extraction, `scopedDerivedId` (a derived record's id in its visibility's partition), `isVisibleWithinScope`, the error semantic search raises when indexing is off, and the list request, search result and projection source role types. It also re-exports, for FAQ capture, `findNearestEntity` (the nearest record a confirmation accepts) and `waitForEmbeddingsToDrain`, the guest-reply and embedding-ready channels, the user permission level schema, the chat message type and the Inbox item, detail, action and actor shapes. It also re-exports `findRelatedEntities`, the entries nearest an origin by stored embeddings over the reads a data source is handed, which the book pages trace themes with. Answers, channels and ready handlers act as the package and are released when it shuts down; a context the runtime did not build is refused. `withAuthAuthority(definition)` makes one service the brain's auth authority: `serviceRuntime(context).authAuthority` binds the auth backend (`bind`), the account-settings registry and backend (`accountSettings.registry`, `bindBackend`, `accountDeleted`), and reads the configured principal seeds and replaces the runtime principal projection (`principals.configuredSeeds`, `replaceRuntimeState`); its bindings are released when the service shuts down, a service that did not declare it is refused, and a second service declaring it in one brain is refused when it registers. `serviceRuntime(context).channelDescriptor(type)` reads one registered channel type's descriptor, as the channel registry reads it.

entries.behavior: Gives a first-party interface converted from a class what the public interface contract does not offer. Through `interfaceRuntime(context)` on its setup, routes and daemons contexts and on its first-party slots: the interface's logger; the brain's agent, a turn in a conversation and the answer to an approval it waits on, as the class reached them through context.agent; a conversation's stored messages; whether a sender stands for the brain's anchor; and, for an interface with a message transport only, the message coordination its class inherited (the input it is answering, which holds job completions back until the reply is out, and job progress a terminal UI follows); answers to first-party contracts under the channels they already have (`email:source-read`), with the sender, released when the interface shuts down; requests to another package's contract, and commands to every package that hears one; the runtime state its class stored under the namespace the class named (`email.inbound.uid-cursor`); a sender's permission level on an interface; whether the brain runs in production, its domain and whether it serves HTTP; the auth backend the brain bound, read when asked; the brain's MCP service for a protocol transport; its endpoint and its way into the brain; a typed channel it hears in the main process, released at shutdown; handlers run once the brain is ready, where the class's onReady ran; the brain's character and anchor profile, its resolved profile kind, its public skills and the tools a permission level may call; read-only entity reads (whether a type is registered, a page, one record) at the scope each call names; the runtime's shared upload store (`upload`, at the route the interface names) and the retirement of a retired upload namespace's directory (nothing beside it, never the shared store); gathered answers to a collect contract; the brain's shared spaces, site URL, local site URL and whether links prefer it; conversations started and messages added for a platform's shared space; whether guest turns can run, the brain's app info, theme stylesheet and preview URL, the route a well-known role names, an operational health check under the interface, an Inbox source, a job's status, and Studio for a workspace it composes from a declared one (never from a worker), shared with the first-party service runtime; conversations read, listed, renamed and deleted as the class did; and, with a message transport, the reply it tracks for a job and the tool completions a reply settles. Beside a public `defineInterface` definition, as plain data and functions: `withDaemon(definition, slot)`, a daemon its class registered, started and stopped under `<plugin id>:<id>` with its own health and no readiness to wait for (`cli:cli`), or none when the slot returns none; `withChannels(definition, slot)`, the channels its class registered, each descriptor as written (subject pattern, manual delivery) with its delivery when it declares one, in the worker as in the main process, which makes the interface a message interface as its class was; `withWebRoutes(definition, slot)`, the HTTP routes its class served as written (any response, with its public, preview, role and match settings), served once it registers after the routes its definition declares; `withTools(definition, slot)`, the tools its class registered under their names as written with their visibility, side effects and MCP exposure; `withProtocolPlugin(definition, protocol, config)`, a protocol-only registration of itself (another definition under the same plugin id and package, configured from the host's config) that the eval harness builds; and `withMessageTransport(definition, slot)`, which runs the runtime's message coordination for the interface and sends job progress and completions through the transport the slot returns, as its class extended the message interface base: rendering progress and completions, sending with an id and editing in place, and routing progress and tool events and the settling of held tool completions through hooks around the runtime's own handling. Its HTTP helpers include the JSON response and the same-origin request checks a web route answers with. For its browser UI, how a reply's artifact cards and confirmation results read and which uploads a composer accepts (`@brains/sdk/internal/message-display`), from modules that import only shared libraries. A context the runtime did not build is refused, a daemon id declared twice is refused, a transport, channels, web routes, tools and a protocol plugin are each declared once, and a definition defineInterface did not return is refused.
entries.currentConsumers: First-party interfaces converted to declarative definitions: the terminal (chat-repl), which answers through the agent with its own conversation and approvals, runs its Ink UI in a class-shaped daemon and shows job progress and completions through a message transport; Email, which registers the email channel with its subject pattern and, when configured, its Resend sender in every process, runs its IMAP listener as its class's daemon only with a mailbox, answers email:source-read, asks inbound-email and auth-principal-resolve, and keeps its IMAP cursor and source locators under its class's namespaces; MCP, which serves /status and /mcp through its own streamable HTTP transport, registers its chat and confirm tools under those names, builds its protocol-only registration for the eval harness, runs its server as mcp:mcp, advertises its endpoint and way in over HTTP, and reads the brain's production flag, domain, whether it serves HTTP, auth backend, MCP service, permission levels and job progress; A2A, which serves its Agent Card (ready once the brain is), agent directory and JSON-RPC endpoint with CORS and SSE on the shared webserver, registers agent_call, answers a2a:ask:request, a2a:call:request and a2a:call:agents, signs and verifies peer requests through the auth backend, keeps its public-ask allowance under a2a.public-asks, and reads the brain's identity, profile kind, public skills, public tools and saved agents; chat, which runs one Chat SDK app for Discord and Slack as chat:chat, registers both platforms' channels in every process, serves their webhooks, keeps uploads in the shared store and deletes its retired discord-chat and slack-chat upload directories once at startup, answers chat:space-notice, gathers space-notice actions, records shared-space conversations, keeps its thread subscriptions under its class's namespaces, and renders, edits and routes job progress and tool statuses through its message transport; web chat, which serves its Ask page, chat API, Ask assets and guest API on the shared host as written, streams replies, job progress and tool statuses to the browser through its message transport, keeps uploads in the shared store at its API path, runs web-chat:guest-maintenance from the scheduler, marks guest chat open once guest turns can run, records its guest state and Ask box availability under its class's namespaces, asks the site builder to build again after each guest switch, reports the guest usage record's health, and registers its guest monitor in Studio once the brain is ready.

entries.behavior: Gives a first-party site package what its embedded runtime plugin registered, beside its public structural definition. `withSiteRuntime(site, { id, config, templates, dataSources })` carries the site's templates, as createTemplate makes them, under the namespace its plugin registered them (`personal-site`), and its fetching data sources under `<id>:<local id>`, read by other packages as `<site package>:<local id>`; both are built from the site's config, its entityDisplay and the brain's site settings parsed by the declared schema, with a conventional site's pluginConfig beneath them. The runtime carries it on the site under a key no field names, through extendSite and the resolver, and registers it once the site package registers. A site data source reaches, through `siteDataSourceRuntime(context)`, the build's entity reads at its scope, the brain's site, preview and local URLs and whether links prefer the local one, the web routes the brain's packages serve, requests to a contract's owner under the site's id, and its logger. A context the runtime did not build for a site is refused.
entries.currentConsumers: The first-party site packages that embedded a runtime plugin: personal, professional (and default, which re-exports it), organization and rizom-ai, for their homepage, about and writing templates and the data sources behind them.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Promote what the sites need to the public site contract (copy overlays, generated sections, runtime scripts and site config on a data source) or retire it when no first-party site does.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: the templates and data sources are registered per boot and store nothing.

entries.behavior: Reads older message metadata and restricts messages that lack provenance.
entries.currentConsumers: Persisted conversations written before provenance metadata became mandatory.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Backfill supported conversations and observe zero messages without canonical provenance.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older conversations remain safely readable during rollback.

entries.behavior: Rejects retired model, preset, or implicit bundle configuration with migration guidance.

entries.behavior: Retains the Drizzle schema needed to migrate databases created by the former vector layout.

entries.behavior: Runs a declared {type}:generation job whose queued data is the entity plugin class handler's raw input (with the entity it fills beside it) rather than the runtime's package-job envelope: the input is checked by the generation's schema and the job runs as the package, since no requester was recorded. Data that names a requester is held to the envelope.

entries.removalPrerequisite: Phase 2 close-out (slice 10): observe zero pending or retrying {type}:generation rows in the raw shape on supported runtime databases.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: a rolled-back class handler reads the raw shape it wrote.

entries.behavior: Atomically retires one explicitly selected pre-scheduler projection job only when it has no attempt ownership, progress, or result.

entries.rollbackDependency: Retained alpha rollback targets can still expose the pre-scheduler rows that block an idle predeploy snapshot.

entries.behavior: Supplies a fallback lease duration for direct dequeue callers that do not pass worker-owned lease settings.

entries.removalPrerequisite: Require explicit lease settings on every supported dequeue caller and observe zero fallback use.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older direct dequeue callers require the fallback while they remain supported.

entries.behavior: Allows registered asset-backed entity types to retain inline binary content while mixed legacy/reference image migration is resumable.
entries.currentConsumers: Existing image rows that still contain data URLs during the image cutover and rollback window.

entries.symbol: frontmatterSchema scalar grammar, colon-string quoting, and binary representation
entries.behavior: Retains YAML 3 frontmatter octal/base-60 numeric meanings, colon-string quoting required by publishing consumers, and binary value representation while using the maintained YAML 4 parser; no executable engines or removed-API fallback.
entries.currentConsumers: Durable and custom frontmatter authored under gray-matter's YAML 3 schema, including external supported content sources.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Approve a durable-frontmatter format migration, verify equivalent values across supported content sources and rollback targets, and observe zero dependence on the previous scalar grammar.
entries.rollbackDependency: Removing the schema without that migration reinterprets bare values such as 012, 0o12, and 12:34 in existing documents.

entries.symbol: FAQ body read path from before the structured content formatter
entries.behavior: Reads FAQ bodies stored with the answer at the top and alternatives as ### sections under "## Alternative answers", FAQ sources stored in frontmatter, and source excerpts kept as "> " quote lines under each source. The next write stores the formatter layout with sources in the body and no quotes.
entries.currentConsumers: FAQs captured in deployed brains before the formatter layout, and their synced files.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored FAQs without an "## Answer" section, with frontmatter sources or with quoted sources across supported upgrade sources, or rewrite them in place.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before the formatter layout cannot read FAQs rewritten in it; they need the forward release.

entries.symbol: LEGACY_IDENTITY: the model of an embedding index written before it recorded its identity
entries.behavior: An embedding index with rows and no embedding_meta row is read as written by openai:text-embedding-3-small at 1536 dimensions and prompt revision 0, so a brain still on that model keeps its index, and one that changed model rebuilds it.
entries.currentConsumers: Embedding indexes of deployed brains written before the index recorded its identity.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe an embedding_meta row in the embedding index of every supported upgrade source.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before the identity record ignores embedding_meta, so after a switch to another embedding model it reads vectors of the wrong dimensions until its index is rebuilt.

exemptions.reason: typescript-legacy is an npm alias used to isolate the compatibility compiler; it is not a persisted or runtime legacy contract.
pdfjs-dist/legacy is an upstream package export path and cannot be renamed locally.
deprecated is dependency-cruiser's dependency type for npm packages their authors deprecated; the rule forbids depending on them.
deprecated is the npm registry's version metadata field; the script verifies that retired packages carry it.
deprecated and deprecatedBy are lifecycle values of published ATProto lexicon metadata; they describe a lexicon's status, not compatibility code here.
